Shanghai Tianfuzhiguo Gourmet World Co., Ltd. v. Shanghai

Hongmofang Club Co., Ltd. — Dispute over compensation for unfair competition

Plaintiff: Shanghai Tianfuzhiguo Gourmet World Co., Ltd.

Legal Representative: Song Xueqin, Chairman.

Agent ad litem: Zhuo Longhua, General Manager.

Agent ad litem: Cao Jiafei, Lawyer of Shanghai Investment and Finance Law Firm.

Defendant: Shanghai Hongmofang Club Co., Ltd.

Legal Representative: Ni Yuanzhen, Chairman.

Agent ad litem: Liu Xueling and Tang Yi, Lawyers of Shanghai Zhongxin Law Firm.

The plaintiff, Shanghai Tianfuzhiguo Gourmet World Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tianfuzhiguo Company), filed a lawsuit with the Shanghai Jing'an District People's Court on the grounds that the defendant, Shanghai Hongmofang Club Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hongmofang Company), had engaged in unfair competition that damaged the plaintiff's interests, requesting the court to order the defendant to eliminate the adverse effects, make a formal apology, compensate for economic losses of RMB 84,360, and bear the litigation costs of this case.

The plaintiff alleged: The defendant opened a hot pot section, recruited the plaintiff's employees, had them wear the plaintiff's uniforms, use the plaintiff's hot pot order forms, and hung a banner stating "Hongmofang Second Floor Hot Pot Section, specially hiring 'Tianfuzhiguo' super-grade hot pot chef, welcome to taste." He Gang, the manager of the defendant's hot pot section, also instigated the plaintiff's male ushers to introduce the plaintiff's customers to the defendant's premises, among other acts, which caused a continuous decline in the plaintiff's business turnover and damaged the plaintiff's interests.

The defendant argued: Recruiting the plaintiff's employees was normal. The uniforms and hot pot order forms did not bear the plaintiff's name or logo. The term "Tianfuzhiguo" in the banner referred to Sichuan Province, not the plaintiff. He Gang, the manager of the hot pot section, only asked the plaintiff's male ushers to introduce customers to the defendant's premises when the plaintiff was fully booked and customers were about to leave, which did not harm the plaintiff's interests. The defendant requested the dismissal of the plaintiff's claims.

The Jing'an District People's Court found through public trial:

The plaintiff, Tianfuzhiguo Company, commenced operations in October 1993, specializing in Sichuan cuisine and hot pot, and was a designated restaurant for tourists in Shanghai. Several news media, including *Xinmin Evening News*, *News Daily*, and Hong Kong's *Ta Kung Pao*, had reported on the plaintiff's business and, in their reports, referred to the plaintiff as "Tianfuzhiguo." The defendant, Hongmofang Company, after recruiting He Gang and seven other former employees of Tianfuzhiguo Company, opened a hot pot section on December 30 of the same year. At a prominent location outside its business premises, it hung a banner reading: "Hongmofang Second Floor Hot Pot Section, specially hiring 'Tianfuzhiguo' super-grade hot pot chef, welcome to taste," and purchased hot pot order forms bearing the plaintiff's marks for use in its external business operations. The banner display and use of the plaintiff's hot pot order forms lasted for over a week. Some of the defendant's service personnel wore the plaintiff's uniforms during business hours for over a month. In addition, the person in charge of the defendant's hot pot section privately requested the plaintiff's male ushers to "pull in customers" for the defendant. The court also found that the plaintiff Tianfuzhiguo Company's business turnover for November 1993, December 1993, and January 1994 was RMB 980,000, RMB 1,020,000, and RMB 770,000, respectively; the defendant Hongmofang Company's business turnover for December 1993 and January 1994 was RMB 60,000 and RMB 140,000, respectively.

The above facts are confirmed by the testimony of witnesses He Gang, Chen Mingyuan, Wu Zhongzhi, Gu Chenglai, Cai Yuebo, Chu Ping, Ni Yuanzhen, and Zhu Maosong; physical evidence provided by the plaintiff Tianfuzhiguo Company, including hot pot order forms, letterheads, and napkins; personnel files and financial statement materials provided by both parties; video footage provided by the plaintiff and video footage of the exteriors of both parties' premises taken by the court.

The Jing'an District People's Court held that the above-mentioned acts of the defendant, Hongmofang Company, constituted unfair competition through misleading and deceptive conduct, violating the relevant provisions of Articles 5 and 9 of the *Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China*. Moreover, the defendant's acts directly resulted in the damage of a decline in the plaintiff's business turnover. To uphold fair competition and lawful business operations and to ensure the healthy development of the socialist market economic order, the defendant shall bear liability for damages in accordance with Article 20 of the *Anti-Unfair Competition Law*. Additionally, it shall bear civil liability pursuant to Items (1), (7), (9), and (10) of Paragraph 1 of Article 134 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China*. Accordingly, on May 19, 1994, the Jing'an District People's Court entered the following judgment:

1. The defendant, Hongmofang Company, shall, within twenty days from the date this judgment takes effect, publish a notice occupying one-sixteenth of a page in a city-level newspaper in Shanghai, apologizing to the plaintiff, Tianfuzhiguo Company, and eliminating the adverse effects. The content of the notice must be approved by the court, and the cost of publication shall be borne by the defendant.

2. The defendant, Hongmofang Company, shall, within ten days from the date this judgment takes effect, compensate the Tianfuzhiguo Company for losses in the amount of RMB 30,000.

After the judgment of first instance was pronounced, neither the plaintiff nor the defendant appealed.
